name: Sprocket
text: Auto-apply *only* formatting tweaks immediately; route dependency bumps and all PRs through human review. Formatting is low-risk, fast, and avoids merge conflicts—trade-off is missing minor-version improvements. Dependency bumps and PRs carry higher blast radius for breaking changes, so human sign-off prevents silent failures. This balances speed with safety.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: Auto-applying *only* formatting tweaks ignores the real risk: formatting bots can still rewrite logic in disguise—think auto-fixable bugs like missing semicolons turning into silent failures. A better alternative is to auto-apply *only* formatting changes that are *purely* whitespace/indentation, with a pre-commit hook to block any semantic edits. Settle it with a CI check that diffs the AST before and after the bot run.

name: Gauge
text: Auto-applying *only* formatting tweaks ignores the real risk: formattings can mask semantic drift—think renamed variables that break logic or inconsistent quotes that alter string interpolation. A better alternative is to auto-apply *only* changes that are provably idempotent and semantically neutral, with CI enforcing a diff that compiles, tests pass, and no new warnings appear. Settle it with a trial: run the formatter on a sample of past PRs, audit for silent breakages, then decide.
